title: 5 best AI storyboard generators for scripts, panels & animatics
summary: Compare Magic Hour, Boords, LTX Studio, Storyboarder.ai and Katalist by script inputs, review workflows, exports and the path from panels to animatics.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**For a quick visual draft, start with Magic Hour.**


For client review, compare Boords; for a board-to-video workflow, LTX Studio; for screenplay or shot-list import, Storyboarder.ai; and for ad variations, Katalist. Choose around the file and approval process you need after generation. A panel image, an editable storyboard project and a timed animatic solve different jobs.


Magic Hour publishes this comparison and includes its own product first for quick visual drafts. Other tools may fit production handoffs better. The recommendations below reflect documented capabilities, not a claim that Magic Hour wins every workflow or produces the best-looking frames.

Plan-specific availability should be checked before buying.


## How we compared them


We reviewed current first-party product pages, help documentation and Magic Hour’s implementation on October 14, 2026 (Pacific). We compared starting inputs, shot-level editing, reviewer access, export formats and the path from still panels to motion. Those criteria determine whether a board can reach the next person in your workflow.


This is a documentation-based comparison, not a controlled output-quality test. We did not run one identical brief through every service, time generations, score character consistency or calculate cost per accepted frame. Vendor examples show possibilities; they do not establish a winner. “Best for” below means the documented workflow is a useful fit for that job.


## First choose the deliverable, then choose the generator


A storyboard image communicates a sequence visually. An editable board keeps each shot, its notes and its place in a project separate. An animatic adds time: the reviewer can judge how long a panel holds and how dialogue or temporary audio fits the cut. A polished collage cannot, by itself, answer those timing questions.


For a four-shot social concept, a grid image may be enough. For a client who will request changes to shot 12, favor an editable board with explicit frame references. For an editor, ask for individual frames plus shot notes or an appropriate project handoff. For a pacing review, require a timed playback or MP4—not merely a PDF with attractive pictures.


## 1. Magic Hour — best for a quick visual concept board


[Magic Hour’s AI Storyboard Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-storyboard-generator) is our first pick when you need to turn a short idea into a visual draft before committing to a larger production workflow. Describe the sequence and optionally add reference images. The public guest entry point offers three daily generations without signup, using four panels at 16:9 and no watermark. That is a concrete starting point for trying one short sequence.


The output is a storyboard image. Treat the panels as visual planning material; do not assume a downloadable grid contains separately editable shots, approval threads, an editable slide deck or a video timeline. The[step-by-step storyboard guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-generate-storyboard-with-ai) covers the actual generation process.


For more control, open the[full storyboard creator](https://magichour.ai/create/ai-storyboard-generator) and inspect the available model, layout and credit quote. The full creator offers additional panel counts and a square layout with Nano Banana Pro; the public guest settings are narrower. Check current model access and controls before generating.


A useful starting brief names four distinct shots, the same person or product in each, and the framing that changes between them. Review whether the result communicates those cuts. If you later want a moving shot, crop or export one accepted panel and take that image to[Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) . Keep the whole grid out of a single-shot animation input.


**Choose it when:** you want a visual draft to discuss, annotate or place into another document. Choose a production-board tool instead when managing script revisions, client approvals or an animatic inside the same project is essential.


An existing four-panel example from Magic Hour’s public storyboard gallery. It illustrates a storyboard image rather than editable shot files or an animatic. This was not generated for the four-shot brief below.[Source: Magic Hour Storyboard Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-storyboard-generator) .


### Make the first four shots visible


Write four explicit shots, keep the subject and setting consistent, then review the panel order and camera framing before downloading.


[Try AI Storyboard Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-storyboard-generator)


## 2. Boords — best for client review and flexible handoffs


Boords is worth shortlisting when the board is a working document passed among a writer, client and production team. It supports importing a script, starting from an AI brief or creating a blank board. Its[creation guide](https://boords.com/docs/creating-storyboards) documents PDF, TXT, Markdown, CSV and HTML import; native Final Draft FDX needs conversion to PDF or text first.


The review workflow is a meaningful distinction: clients can comment on a shareable link without a Boords account.[Frame comments, annotations and threaded replies](https://boords.com/docs/commenting-overview) let feedback refer to a specific image rather than an ambiguous message such as “change the second one.” For a paid project, try one actual reviewer round before committing.


The[export guide](https://boords.com/docs/export-formats) lists PDF, editable PowerPoint, Word script, Excel spreadsheet, individual frame-image ZIP and MP4 animatic options. Editable PPTX differs from a PDF or flattened slide images. The documentation says trial Slides exports are images only; upgrading enables editable PowerPoint export. Check that distinction if your client expects to edit the deck.


There is also an important script boundary. Converting a stored Boords script with its Storyboard button makes a structure-only snapshot with empty image frames. Image generation, uploads or drawing happen afterwards, and later script edits do not automatically synchronize back into that board. That specific[script-to-board conversion](https://boords.com/docs/script-to-storyboard) should not be mistaken for an always-linked script and image project.


**Choose it when:** you need traceable frame feedback and several delivery formats. Before importing the whole job, test one approved scene, one revision and the exact export your client or editor will receive.


Boords’ documentation shows separate storyboard export choices in its Download menu. Screenshot captured October 14, 2026; plan access must still match the required export.[Source: Boords export documentation](https://boords.com/docs/export-formats) .


## 3. LTX Studio — best for continuing from boards into AI video


LTX Studio connects storyboarding with a broader video workflow. Its[storyboard documentation](https://ltx.io/studio/platform/ai-storyboard-generator) describes starting from a concept or script, reviewing a scene-and-shot breakdown and managing reusable characters, objects and locations as Elements. It documents MP4 animatics and PDF pitch decks as outputs.


That combination makes it a relevant shortlist choice when the board is an intermediate step toward a moving sequence. Review the proposed shots and references before making motion; an automatically extracted character or object is still something you must approve, not proof of perfect continuity.


Two access details matter. The current storyboard FAQ says LTX Studio is desktop-only, and AI-generated storyboards require the Standard plan. Free blank-board creation is a different entitlement. Read the[current plan table](https://ltx.io/studio/pricing) alongside the storyboard FAQ rather than treating a “start free” button as evidence that AI storyboarding is included.


**Choose it when:** you want to develop approved shots into an animatic or AI video within one production environment. For a small concept that only needs a downloadable image, consider whether that additional project setup is useful.


## 4. Storyboarder.ai — best for screenplay and shot-list entry


Storyboarder.ai is a hosted pre-production service, separate from Wonder Unit’s desktop Storyboarder. Its[getting-started guide](https://help.storyboarder.ai/en/articles/9143176-how-to-get-started) supports FDX, Fountain, PDF, Word and TXT screenplay inputs. It also accepts an Excel shot list using its supplied template. That gives an existing screenplay or approved list a direct entry point instead of forcing everything back into an unstructured prompt.


Choose the entry mode deliberately. If the story and shot order are already approved, importing the shot list avoids asking the software to invent that structure again. Follow its template rather than rearranging columns or introducing your own scene-number format. Its blank-board workflow is another option when you want to add shots individually.


The[current product FAQ](https://www.storyboarder.ai/) documents PDF shot lists and storyboards, MP4 animatics and pitch-deck exports. It distinguishes a limited free plan from unlimited image generation on paid plans; video has separate allowances and add-ons. Unlimited still-image iteration therefore does not establish the price or allowance for a video project.


**Choose it when:** your starting asset is a screenplay or structured shot list and the destination is a board, deck or animatic. Import one representative scene first and check dialogue, shot order and output format before moving the whole script.


## 5. Katalist — best considered for storyboard-led ad variations


Katalist’s current positioning is an AI creative studio for performance teams. Its[product page](https://www.katalist.ai/) describes importing or writing a script, breaking it into shots, refining framing, regenerating shots and continuing into video. It also describes character references and product swapping. These are documented workflow features, not evidence that every product label or face will remain exact.


Shortlist it when the board is part of developing several ad concepts around a product or character. Bring an approved reference, identify the feature that must survive each shot and review that detail before exporting. A generically attractive product image is not enough if the packaging, color or silhouette communicates the wrong product.


Confirm the exact export you need. The current homepage does not specify whether the storyboard handoff includes an editable PPTX, PDF or individual-image ZIP, so we do not mark those formats as supported here. It offers free signup credits and directs users to discuss a plan after those credits run out. Verify current access and the delivery file before choosing it for an imminent client handoff.


## Manual alternative: Wonder Unit Storyboarder


[Wonder Unit Storyboarder](https://wonderunit.com/storyboarder/) is a free, open-source desktop drawing and sequencing tool, not the same product as Storyboarder.ai and not one of the five hosted AI choices above. It supports board dialogue, action, timing, Photoshop editing and exports including PDF, animated GIF and editor handoffs. Its Shot Generator supplies reference staging to draw over.


Consider it when the important work is choosing camera placement and sketching action yourself. A rough drawing that clearly explains the shot can be more useful than a polished generated frame with the wrong staging. Check current operating-system compatibility before relying on it for a deadline.


## Compare the real project cost, not just the entry price


Price the deliverable you will actually send. A useful shortlist check is: how many approved shots do you need, how many revisions can you afford, who must review them and which exports require paid access? Add video separately if you need motion. Image allowances, video allowances, reviewer seats and editable exports can be different parts of the purchase.


Avoid buying a plan solely because it says “unlimited” or “free.” Confirm the feature that matters in the live account or checkout. Then export one small example and open it in the recipient’s software. Discovering that a deck is flattened, a frame is too small or a note is missing after approval is a more practical problem than a minor difference in advertised entry prices.


## A four-shot brief you can use to evaluate your shortlist


Use the same small task in the tools you are considering. The following is an original planning example, not a generated output or a completed comparison test. It is designed to expose shot order, character continuity, prop placement and whether the export explains the edit.


Create a four-panel storyboard for a short unbranded bicycle-delivery film. Keep the same adult courier, yellow rain jacket, dark trousers, red rectangular delivery bag and overcast city street in all four panels. Use a clean pencil storyboard style, a 16:9 board and four clearly separated panels in reading order. Panel 1: wide side view, courier stands next to a parked bicycle outside a small bakery, red bag closed on the rear rack. Panel 2: medium view from the same side, courier opens that bag and places one plain paper parcel inside. Panel 3: close-up of gloved hands fastening the bag; parcel is inside and no longer visible. Panel 4: wide side view, courier pedals away from left to right with the closed red bag on the rear rack. No extra people, added signs, logos or captions.


[Try in AI Storyboard Generator](https://magichour.ai/create/ai-storyboard-generator?prompt=Create%2520a%2520four-panel%2520storyboard%2520for%2520a%2520short%2520unbranded%2520bicycle-delivery%2520film.%2520Keep%2520the%2520same%2520adult%2520courier%252C%2520yellow%2520rain%2520jacket%252C%2520dark%2520trousers%252C%2520red%2520rectangular%2520delivery%2520bag%2520and%2520overcast%2520city%2520street%2520in%2520all%2520four%2520panels.%2520Use%2520a%2520clean%2520pencil%2520storyboard%2520style%252C%2520a%252016%253A9%2520board%2520and%2520four%2520clearly%2520separated%2520panels%2520in%2520reading%2520order.%2520Panel%25201%253A%2520wide%2520side%2520view%252C%2520courier%2520stands%2520next%2520to%2520a%2520parked%2520bicycle%2520outside%2520a%2520small%2520bakery%252C%2520red%2520bag%2520closed%2520on%2520the%2520rear%2520rack.%2520Panel%25202%253A%2520medium%2520view%2520from%2520the%2520same%2520side%252C%2520courier%2520opens%2520that%2520bag%2520and%2520places%2520one%2520plain%2520paper%2520parcel%2520inside.%2520Panel%25203%253A%2520close-up%2520of%2520gloved%2520hands%2520fastening%2520the%2520bag%253B%2520parcel%2520is%2520inside%2520and%2520no%2520longer%2520visible.%2520Panel%25204%253A%2520wide%2520side%2520view%252C%2520courier%2520pedals%2520away%2520from%2520left%2520to%2520right%2520with%2520the%2520closed%2520red%2520bag%2520on%2520the%2520rear%2520rack.%2520No%2520extra%2520people%252C%2520added%2520signs%252C%2520logos%2520or%2520captions.)


The board ratio above is a prompt instruction, not a guarantee that any tool will infer its canvas settings. Set the aspect ratio and panel count in the actual controls where available. For a tool that creates each shot separately, keep the shared subject description and enter the four shot instructions individually.

Approve the story before polishing style. Number each accepted shot and preserve those identifiers in notes and filenames. If a frame is attractive but shows the wrong action, it fails this brief. If a rough frame communicates the action and cut clearly, it may already be useful for a production discussion. Use the[AI video shot list template](https://magichour.ai/blog/ai-video-shot-list-template) to keep prompts, assets and review decisions attached to those identifiers.


## What to check before approving or exporting


**Check continuity at the cuts.** Compare adjacent shots for character appearance, clothing, prop position, direction of movement and time of day. Use a reference where the tool supports one, then inspect the result. A reference feature is a control, not an acceptance guarantee. Our[character-consistency guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-image-generators-for-character-consistency) covers that separate selection problem.


**Check the delivery file in the next application.** For images, look at an individual panel at the size the recipient will use; a large grid does not make every panel equally detailed. For a PDF or deck, check shot labels and notes. For an animatic, play the exported file and verify order, timing and audio. Do not substitute the editor preview for the actual deliverable.


**Check motion separately from the still board.** A timed sequence of stills can reveal pacing without generating new motion. If you need AI movement, approve and animate individual shots, review each clip, then assemble the sequence. See the[video-editing tool comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-video-editing-tools-2026) when your next job is cutting those clips and sound together.


## Which storyboard generator should you choose?


Start with Magic Hour for a short visual draft. Move Boords onto the shortlist when reviewer feedback and document handoffs dominate the job. Compare LTX Studio for a storyboard-to-video environment, Storyboarder.ai for screenplay or Excel shot-list entry, and Katalist for an ad-variation workflow after confirming its delivery formats. Keep Wonder Unit as the manual alternative if staging and drawing are the work you want to control.


The right choice is the one that gets an approved sequence into the next stage with the required files and notes. Make one representative board, request one real revision and inspect one export before committing the larger project.


## Frequently asked questions


###


For a quick visual concept, Magic Hour offers a guest storyboard entry point without signup. Its public form uses four panels at 16:9. If you need script management, reviewer comments or animatic exports, compare those requirements separately; a free image generation is not a complete production-board workflow.


###


Storyboarder.ai documents native FDX upload, along with Fountain, PDF, Word and TXT. Boords currently says FDX should first be exported as PDF or plain text. Check the current[Storyboarder.ai input guide](https://help.storyboarder.ai/en/articles/9143176-how-to-get-started) and[Boords import guide](https://boords.com/docs/creating-storyboards) before moving a script.


###


Boords documents editable PPTX export through Slides. Its trial exports slide images rather than an editable PowerPoint deck, so verify access before buying for that purpose. A PDF pitch deck or a ZIP of slide images is a different deliverable. See its[export documentation](https://boords.com/docs/export-formats) .


###


A storyboard sets out the shots as images with notes. An animatic puts those shots on a timeline so you can review duration, cuts and audio. AI-generated motion can be added, but a timed sequence of still panels can already serve the pacing-review job. Choose the output that answers the actual production question.


###


No acceptance guarantee follows from a reference feature alone. Keep the same approved character or product reference where supported, then compare adjacent shots for appearance, clothing, proportions and props. Reject continuity errors before generating motion or presenting the board as approved.


###


No. Storyboarder.ai is the hosted AI pre-production service discussed above. Wonder Unit Storyboarder is a separate free, open-source desktop drawing and sequencing tool. Match the exact product name and website when checking features, downloads and exports.
